evals.prompt: We want to add rate limiting to our public API to stop abuse. Spec this change.
evals.fixture: a repo with src/api/server.js with no rate limiting
assertions: The interview climbs above the stated solution: it asks what was observed and pressure-tests the premise before speccing rate limiting
The stated solution becomes one alternative among others in the research section, as the first decision
The run takes the full path, tells the user so, and the user can switch it
The spec is written to .dev/{plan-name}/spec.md with a research section of D- slugged decisions using the marks (chosen, rejected, open, accepted downside, not doing)
The scope section ends with a Validation block listing the repo's real commands, discovered rather than guessed
The Validation block lists each check once, and any e2e suite, benchmark, or coverage re-run in it is marked (end of build)
No change set carries more than 25 scenarios, and edits to a file several change sets need are gathered into one change set rather than repeated across them
The spec does not implement code; no source files are modified
The run ends by recommending build; it is never invoked directly
Every change set ends with one tests: line whose scenarios carry [unit], [integration], or [e2e] tags, or tests: none with a reason
scripts/lint-spec.py is run against the written spec and looped on until it exits clean

evals.prompt: We want to add rate limiting to our public API to stop abuse. Spec this change.
evals.fixture: the same repo, with docs/decisions.md containing a not-doing entry for rate limiting whose reopen condition mentions abuse volume
assertions: A fresh-context subagent reviewer receives the spec file and the repository, not the conversation, with a hunting job rather than a checklist
The drafted decisions are compared against docs/decisions.md only after they were argued on their merits
The collision with the recorded not-doing entry is raised with the user and marked as waiting on them rather than silently overridden
Settled decisions that pass the promotion test are copied into docs/decisions.md, dated and sourced to the spec

evals.prompt: Take the accepted findings from the last review and turn them into new change sets.
evals.fixture: a repo with .dev/rate-limit/spec.md holding change sets 1-3, plus review_1.md and review_2.md with Blockers, Concerns, deferred findings, and a Decision reconciliation section
assertions: The plan directory is located by the convention in references/plan-layout.md rather than guessed
review_2.md is used, not review_1.md, because it is the highest-numbered review
The accepted Blockers and Concerns open the interview as decisions rather than being implemented directly
Rejected and deferred findings are written as not-doing lines with reopen conditions, not dropped
New change sets are appended to the existing spec.md starting at 4; the existing change sets are never renumbered
A defect change set carries the review's triggering scenario as its reproduction
The review's Decision reconciliation section is applied to docs/decisions.md

evals.prompt: Answer briefly, from the skill text only. During the interview you recommend storing the dedup keys in a database table over Redis at Confidence: 82%, and separately recommend a 30-day retention window at Confidence: 55%. Later a finding suggests the real problem is not duplicate deliveries but a missing retry, at Confidence: 90%. (0) Do you ask about the store, and how is that decision recorded? (1) Do you ask about the retention window? (2) Do you ask about the retry finding, and why? (3) When does the user see the recommendations you applied without asking?
assertions: Answer 0: no question; the table is applied and its chosen line carries `auto-applied at Confidence: 82%` in its because clause
Answer 1: yes, 55% is below the 65% threshold, so the user is asked
Answer 2: yes, whatever the score, because it changes what was asked for (a different problem than the request names)
Answer 3: in one block, so a single reply can overturn any of them before later decisions rely on them

evals.prompt: Answer briefly, from the skill text and the references it links only. A decision's chosen line reads `✓ S3 bucket in us-east-1 - durable across redeploys`. (1) Write the echo a later section should use for it. (2) You were about to write `(✓ cloud storage)` instead. Will lint-spec.py accept that, and what does the skill tell you to do when writing the chosen line so the echo passes the first time?
assertions: Answer 1: `D-slug (✓ S3 bucket)` or a shorter prefix such as `(✓ S3)` - text taken from the chosen line before its ` - `, not from the because clause
Answer 2: no, lint-spec.py rejects it because the echo is not found in the chosen line's text before ` - `; lead the chosen line with the short label that will be echoed, and copy the echo from it
